name: topic
description: A Kafka topic, a container of the system. Its key is the broker kind, ':' and the topic name, such as kafka:payments.completed.

name: queue
description: A message queue, a container of the system. Its key is the broker kind (rabbitmq or jms), ':' and the queue or JMS destination name, such as rabbitmq:payments.order-events.

name: exchange
description: A RabbitMQ exchange, a container of the system, routing messages to the queues bound to it. Its key is rabbitmq, ':' and the exchange name, such as rabbitmq:shop.orders.

name: database
description: A database that units' datasources point to, a data store and so a container. Its key is the server (host and port, as the URL gives them), '/' and the database name, such as shop-db:5432/shop, so units on the same database share it; an embedded database without a server is keyed by its unit's key instead.

name: message-broker
description: A message broker server a unit's config connects to, such as a Kafka cluster or a RabbitMQ server. Its key is the broker technology, ':' and its addresses, such as kafka:kafka:9092. It is a container, a server that runs, though container diagrams show its topics, queues and exchanges, never one broker box.

name: external-system
description: A software system outside the snapshot that a unit calls, found from a URL whose host has a domain and names no unit, from the mail server a unit's config names (spring.mail.host), or from the identity provider a unit's config or code names (ADR 0085). Its key is the host, such as sandbox.paygate.example.com or smtp.gmail.com, or for an identity provider a deployment runs, its product (keycloak); the hosts the same call reaches under other profiles are separate systems, named by the call's alternates.

name: person
description: A kind of person who uses the system, as far as the code shows (ADR 0074): a role it checks, the members of something it has members of, those it invites, or the user who signs up and in. Its key is the person's name in lower case with dashes, such as organization-member. Always inferred; never invented beyond what the code names.

name: person-basis
description: What a person rests on: the value is role (a role the code checks), member (members of something), invited (those invited) or account (the user who signs up and in). A person is always inferred from the code.

description.description: One sentence in the code's words saying what shows the person, with the screens of frontends for it.

cites.description: The IDs of the facts the person rests on, the first few.

repos.description: The repositories whose files show the person, sorted.

frontends.description: The repositories of frontends that have screens for the person, sorted.

name: infrastructure
description: A service discovery, config or tracing server outside the snapshot that a unit's config connects to. Its key is its host and port, such as config:8888. It is a container, a server that runs, though diagrams keep infrastructure apart from the business dependencies.

name: RESOLVES_TO
description: The subject, a destination or address keyed by its module and the expression its code writes, is the object, the literal destination or address, in a view: the default view, the profile named, or the deployment named, whose container's environment overlays the config as Spring Boot's relaxed binding reads it (#588), when the module's config resolves every placeholder of the expression (ADR 0094, amendment for #587). One fact for the default view, which names in exceptProfiles and exceptDeployments the views it does not hold in, and one for each profile or deployment that gives another literal; a placeholder's own default resolves it too. Not given where a placeholder stays unresolved or a secret is used. Address resolution (#589) also writes it for each address a matcher asks about, with from naming the unit that uses it: to the unit it leads to, the external system, or outcome:ambiguous or outcome:unknown, one fact for the config's answer and one for each deployment that fills the address in; and with by: name, to each unit a service name names, or outcome:unknown when none does.

profile.description: The profile whose config gives this literal; absent for the default view.

facts.description: The IDs of the config-value facts the expression was resolved with and, in a deployment's view, of the deployment-container fact.

deployment.description: The deployment whose environment gives this literal: <repository>|<platform>|<environment>[|<compose file>]|<container>; absent for the default view and a profile's.

exceptDeployments.description: On the default view's fact, the deployments whose environment gives another literal or none.

exceptProfiles.description: On the default view's fact, the profiles whose config gives another literal or none.

resolved.description: The expression as config resolved it, when that is not the literal's own key: a URL whose address is its host, or a JDBC URL whose address is its server.

from.description: Address resolution: the unit that uses the address, absent for a frontend.

address.description: Address resolution: the address asked about, as the unit's config resolved it, or the service name asked about.

written.description: Address resolution: the address as written, when config changed it.

by.description: Address resolution: name for a service name looked up among the units' spring.application.name; absent for an address.

matched.description: Address resolution: the address as it was matched, filled in where a deployment's environment filled it.

matchedBy.description: Address resolution: how the unit was found (host, container-host, artifact-id, published-port, port, service-name).

factor.description: Address resolution: the confidence factor of the way the unit was found.

fact.description: Address resolution: the ID of the fact the unit was found by, absent for a default port.

filledBy.description: Address resolution: the ID of the deployment-container fact whose environment filled the address in.

order.description: Address resolution: the answer's place among the address's answers, the config's first.

candidates.description: Address resolution, for outcome:ambiguous: each unit it may lead to, with unit, fact (when one), matchedBy and factor.

name: CALLS_HTTP
description: The subject unit or frontend calls the object unit or external system over HTTP. One fact per call in the code and endpoint matched, one per gateway route that sends requests to it (route set), and for a frontend one per URL its code calls from the browser and one per proxy of its server that no call goes through.

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts the link comes from, on both ends and in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone the link holds, so it is conditional. Absent when it holds in the default view.

protocol.description: The protocol, as a line between containers names it: JSON/HTTP, JSON/HTTPS, HTTP, HTTPS, WebSocket (a gateway route to ws://, wss:// or lb:ws://), AMQP, Kafka, JMS, JDBC or R2DBC.

source.description: The entity ID of the code on the subject's side: the method making the call, sending or listening, or declaring the binding; for a gateway route, the method that builds it or the module whose config defines it.

target.description: The entity ID of the code on the object's side: the endpoint's handler method, or the listener method; for a WebSocket gateway route, the method that registers the one WebSocket endpoint it reaches.

client.description: The HTTP client: feign, rest-template, rest-client, web-client, and so on.

path.description: The request path, after the URL's authority or a leading placeholder.

url.description: The URL the call goes to in the view the link was found in, when its host is known.

endpoint.description: The endpoint matched, such as GET /api/products/{id}; for a WebSocket gateway route, the path of the one WebSocket endpoint it reaches, such as /ws-notifications.

endpoints.description: For a WebSocket gateway route that reaches more than one WebSocket endpoint of its target, their paths.

proxy.description: For a frontend's link, the path prefix of the proxy it goes through: the nginx that serves the frontend, or its development server.

navigation.description: For a frontend's link, true when its code navigates the browser to the URL rather than requesting it from the page.

reaches.description: For a frontend's call, the method that handles it: the endpoint's handler, or the method that registers the WebSocket endpoint, of the unit in reachesUnit (ADR 0047, amendment for #331).

reachesUnit.description: For a frontend's call that reaches an endpoint, the unit that serves it: the linked unit itself, or the unit the gateway route in throughRoute sends it to.

reachesEndpoint.description: For a frontend's call that reaches an endpoint, the endpoint as that unit serves it, such as POST /api/auth/sign-in, or the WebSocket endpoint's path.

throughRoute.description: For a frontend's call to a gateway, the id of the gateway route that sends it on to reachesUnit.

route.description: The id of the gateway route the link is, for a link from a Spring Cloud Gateway route.

paths.description: The path patterns of the gateway route, such as /api/users/**.

methods.description: The HTTP methods the gateway route takes; absent when it takes any.

matchedBy.description: How the target was found: service-name (a Feign client's name, or a gateway route's lb:// name, against spring.application.name), host (the URL's host against it), artifact-id (the host against the unit's artifact ID), path (a call to this machine, by its path alone), port (a gateway route or a frontend's call to this machine, by its port against the unit's server.port), published-port (a frontend's call to this machine or a private address, by the port a deployment container that runs the unit publishes), container-host (a frontend's URL host against the names of a deployment container that runs the unit), external (a host with a domain that names no unit) or llm (picked by the LLM resolver among the candidates of a link static matching left open).

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which a link found in the default view does not hold, because the code or config of one of its ends is different or switched off there. Absent when it holds under every profile.

alternates.description: The entity IDs of the other units or external systems the same call reaches under other profiles, such as a production host for a sandbox one.

resolves.description: The claim ID of the unresolved-link the LLM resolver picked this link for. Present only on links of origin llm.

rationale.description: Why the LLM resolver picked this candidate, in its own words. Present only on links of origin llm.

model.description: The provider and model that picked this link, as provider/model. Present only on links of origin llm.

name: PUBLISHES
description: The subject unit sends messages to the object topic, queue or exchange.

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts the link comes from, on both ends and in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone the link holds, so it is conditional. Absent when it holds in the default view.

protocol.description: The protocol, as a line between containers names it: JSON/HTTP, JSON/HTTPS, HTTP, HTTPS, AMQP, Kafka, JMS, JDBC or R2DBC.

source.description: The entity ID of the code on the subject's side: the method making the call, sending or listening, or declaring the binding.

routingKey.description: The routing key a RabbitMQ send gives.

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which a link found in the default view does not hold, because the code or config of one of its ends is different or switched off there. Absent when it holds under every profile.

name: CONSUMES
description: The subject unit listens on the object topic or queue.

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts the link comes from, on both ends and in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone the link holds, so it is conditional. Absent when it holds in the default view.

protocol.description: The protocol, as a line between containers names it: JSON/HTTP, JSON/HTTPS, HTTP, HTTPS, AMQP, Kafka, JMS, JDBC or R2DBC.

source.description: The entity ID of the code on the subject's side: the method making the call, sending or listening, or declaring the binding.

pattern.description: The topic pattern the listener names, when the object topic matches it.

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which a link found in the default view does not hold, because the code or config of one of its ends is different or switched off there. Absent when it holds under every profile.

name: ROUTES_TO
description: The subject exchange routes messages to the object queue, by a binding declared in a unit's code.

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts the link comes from, on both ends and in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone the link holds, so it is conditional. Absent when it holds in the default view.

protocol.description: The protocol, as a line between containers names it: JSON/HTTP, JSON/HTTPS, HTTP, HTTPS, AMQP, Kafka, JMS, JDBC or R2DBC.

source.description: The entity ID of the code on the subject's side: the method making the call, sending or listening, or declaring the binding.

bindingKey.description: The binding's routing key or pattern, AMQP wildcards included.

exchangeType.description: The exchange's type, if known: topic, direct, fanout or headers.

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which a link found in the default view does not hold, because the code or config of one of its ends is different or switched off there. Absent when it holds under every profile.

name: SENDS_MESSAGES_TO
description: Messages the subject unit sends reach a listener of the object unit, asynchronously: the link between containers a queue or topic carries. One fact per send and listener matched.

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts the link comes from, on both ends and in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone the link holds, so it is conditional. Absent when it holds in the default view.

protocol.description: The protocol, as a line between containers names it: JSON/HTTP, JSON/HTTPS, HTTP, HTTPS, AMQP, Kafka, JMS, JDBC or R2DBC.

source.description: The entity ID of the code on the subject's side: the method making the call, sending or listening, or declaring the binding.

target.description: The entity ID of the code on the object's side: the endpoint's handler method, or the listener method.

destination.description: The entity ID of the topic, queue or exchange sent to.

queue.description: The entity ID of the queue the listener receives from, when an exchange routes to it.

bindingKey.description: The binding pattern the routing key matched.

pattern.description: The topic pattern the listener names, when the topic matched it.

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which a link found in the default view does not hold, because the code or config of one of its ends is different or switched off there. Absent when it holds under every profile.

resolves.description: The claim ID of the unresolved-link the LLM resolver picked this link for. Present only on links of origin llm.

rationale.description: Why the LLM resolver picked this candidate, in its own words. Present only on links of origin llm.

model.description: The provider and model that picked this link, as provider/model. Present only on links of origin llm.

name: USES_DATABASE
description: The subject unit connects to the object database through a datasource in its config.

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts the link comes from, on both ends and in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone the link holds, so it is conditional. Absent when it holds in the default view.

protocol.description: The protocol, as a line between containers names it: JSON/HTTP, JSON/HTTPS, HTTP, HTTPS, AMQP, Kafka, JMS, JDBC or R2DBC.

key.description: The config key that sets it.

schemas.description: The entity IDs of the schemas the unit's migrations build.

server.description: A Redis server as the config names it, host:port, or a sentinel or cluster's nodes.

ssl.description: Present and true when the Redis connection uses TLS.

defaulted.description: Present and true when no config names the Redis server and Spring Boot's default, localhost:6379, is taken because the unit's code or a dependency uses Redis.

inferred.description: Why the link rests on an inference: the Redis host or port is a placeholder no config resolves, so units that write the same placeholders are taken to share one server; or the database's name is left to the environment, and of the databases its server creates in a deployment the one whose name shares a word with the unit or the placeholder is taken.

uses.description: The kinds of Redis use the unit's code or config shows: template, hash, session, rate-limiter, lock, cache, pubsub or client.

stores.description: What the unit keeps in Redis, where the code shows it: for each kind of use and key, its kind, key or channel or hash name, data structure, time to live and operations (read, write, delete, lock, other).

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which a link found in the default view does not hold, because the code or config of one of its ends is different or switched off there. Absent when it holds under every profile.

deployments.description: Where the deployments put a datasource whose server or database is a placeholder no config resolves: for each environment that runs the unit, its environment, the container that runs the unit, the container the database is on, the server as the environment writes it (address) and the database's name, when known.

name: ACCESSES_DATA_OF
description: The subject unit's code reads or writes tables that the object unit's schema declares, on a database both use: the two share data, not only a server.

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts the link comes from, on both ends and in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone the link holds, so it is conditional. Absent when it holds in the default view.

protocol.description: The protocol, as a line between containers names it: JSON/HTTP, JSON/HTTPS, HTTP, HTTPS, AMQP, Kafka, JMS, JDBC or R2DBC.

database.description: The entity ID of the database they share.

reads.description: The entity IDs of the object's tables the subject reads.

writes.description: The entity IDs of the object's tables the subject writes.

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which a link found in the default view does not hold, because the code or config of one of its ends is different or switched off there. Absent when it holds under every profile.

name: SENDS_MAIL
description: The subject unit sends mail through the object external system, the mail server its config names (spring.mail.host). One fact per method that sends mail; a unit whose config names a mail server but whose code sends none the extractor recognises has one without source.

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts the link comes from: the mail-send fact and the config values, in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone the link holds, so it is conditional. Absent when it holds in the default view.

protocol.description: SMTP, or SMTPS when spring.mail.protocol says smtps or the port is 465.

source.description: The entity ID of the method that sends the mail. Absent when only the config shows mail is sent.

host.description: The mail server's host, from spring.mail.host.

port.description: The mail server's port, from spring.mail.port, if set.

key.description: The config key that names the host.

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which a link found in the default view does not hold, because the code or config of one of its ends is different or switched off there. Absent when it holds under every profile.

name: USES_IDENTITY_PROVIDER
description: The subject unit uses the object as its identity provider: another unit of the snapshot (an auth service whose JWK set it fetches), or an external system (an issuer on a host with a domain, or one a deployment runs from an identity provider's image, such as Keycloak in compose). Found from spring.security.oauth2.* (resource server issuer-uri and jwk-set-uri, client providers and registrations), keys ending like them (jwk-set-uri, issuer-uri), keycloak.auth-server-url and Keycloak's admin client (ADR 0085). One fact per unit, provider and purpose.

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts the link comes from: the config values that name the provider, the admin client, and what the provider was found by (a unit's name or port, a deployment container), in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone the link holds, so it is conditional. Absent when it holds in the default view.

purpose.description: What the unit does with the provider: validates-tokens (checks the tokens it is sent with the provider's keys), signs-in-users (an OAuth2 or OIDC login), gets-tokens (client credentials or another grant) or manages-users (an admin client).

protocol.description: OIDC, JWKS, OAuth2 or the admin API (Keycloak Admin REST), over HTTP or HTTPS.

url.description: The provider's URL as the unit's config gives it in the view.

key.description: The config key that names the URL, when it is config.

source.description: The entity ID of the method that builds the admin client, for manages-users.

target.description: The entity ID of the endpoint of the target unit the URL's path reaches, such as its JWK set's handler.

matchedBy.description: How the provider was found: host (a unit's spring.application.name), port (a unit's server.port, for this machine), container (a deployment container of an identity provider's image answering the host), published-port (one publishing the port of this machine), provider-name (a provider Spring Security knows by name, such as google) or external (a host with a domain).

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which a link found in the default view does not hold, because the code or config of one of its ends is different or switched off there. Absent when it holds under every profile.

name: USES_BROKER
description: The subject unit's config connects it to the object message broker.

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts the link comes from, on both ends and in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone the link holds, so it is conditional. Absent when it holds in the default view.

protocol.description: The protocol, as a line between containers names it: JSON/HTTP, JSON/HTTPS, HTTP, HTTPS, AMQP, Kafka, JMS, JDBC or R2DBC.

technology.description: The broker, such as Kafka or RabbitMQ.

key.description: The config key that sets the address.

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which a link found in the default view does not hold, because the code or config of one of its ends is different or switched off there. Absent when it holds under every profile.

name: USES_INFRASTRUCTURE
description: The subject unit uses the object service for infrastructure, not business: service discovery, a config server or tracing.

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts the link comes from, on both ends and in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone the link holds, so it is conditional. Absent when it holds in the default view.

protocol.description: The protocol, as a line between containers names it: JSON/HTTP, JSON/HTTPS, HTTP, HTTPS, AMQP, Kafka, JMS, JDBC or R2DBC.

technology.description: Such as Eureka, Consul, ZooKeeper, Spring Cloud Config, Zipkin or OpenTelemetry.

key.description: The config key that names it.

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which a link found in the default view does not hold, because the code or config of one of its ends is different or switched off there. Absent when it holds under every profile.

name: display-name
description: The name documents show for the subject, where its key does not read as one. A unit's own database (an embedded one, or one whose server or database is a placeholder no config resolves) gets its database name when written out, else the one a deployment names, else the unit's name and 'database'; a Redis data store is named Redis, with its server when the snapshot has several; a person is named in the code's words; a frontend takes the name of the compose service that builds it from its folder; an identity provider a deployment runs is named by its product (Keycloak).

name: unresolved-link
description: A call, send or datasource of the subject unit that static matching cannot link: a URL or destination with a placeholder nothing resolves, a call that several units could serve, or a routing key not known. The value is the call, destination or URL as far as it is known. The LLM resolver picks among the candidates; what stays open goes to the questions queue.

kind.description: http, message, database or route (a gateway route).

reason.description: unresolved-placeholder, unknown-url, unknown-host (a host without a domain that names no unit, such as a compose or discovery name), ambiguous, no-match (a call to this machine no unit serves) or unknown-routing-key.

source.description: The entity ID of the code or module it is written in: for a gateway route, the method that builds it or the module whose config defines it.

site.description: Which of the code's or module's links it is, where the source alone does not tell: route and the route's id for a gateway route, or the send or listener predicate and the destination as written for a message. Absent for a call or datasource. A key attribute, so two open links of one source are two claims (#576).

unresolved.description: The keys of the placeholders nothing resolved.

candidates.description: The entity IDs of the units it might link to.

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts the link comes from, on both ends and in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone the link holds, so it is conditional. Absent when it holds in the default view.

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which a link found in the default view does not hold, because the code or config of one of its ends is different or switched off there. Absent when it holds under every profile.

name: unrouted-endpoint
description: An endpoint of a unit the subject gateway routes requests to that none of the gateway's routes to that unit reaches, by path (after StripPrefix and PrefixPath) and HTTP method, so a request to it through the gateway finds no route. The value is the endpoint, such as GET /api/organizations/{id}/preview. Not recorded for a unit a route reaches through a filter that rewrites paths otherwise.

target.description: The entity ID of the unit that serves the endpoint.

endpoint.description: The entity ID of the endpoint's handler method.

calledBy.description: The entity IDs of the units whose HTTP calls the linker matched to the endpoint, so it is reached inside the system; absent when none.

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts it comes from: the endpoint and the gateway's routes to the unit, in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone it holds. Absent when it holds in the default view.

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which it does not hold. Absent when it holds under every profile.

name: routed-endpoint
description: An endpoint of a unit the subject gateway routes requests to, with the request as the gateway receives it: the endpoint's path behind the target's context and servlet paths, through the route's StripPrefix, PrefixPath and RewritePath filters in reverse, or, when no route reaches it and the gateway's discovery locator is on, under the target's service ID. The value is the request, such as POST /profile/profile/admin/users. A flow that starts at the endpoint starts at the gateway with it (ADR 0047, amendment for #351).

target.description: The entity ID of the unit that serves the endpoint.

endpoint.description: The entity ID of the endpoint's handler method.

served.description: The request as the target serves it, such as POST /api/profile/admin/users.

route.description: The id of the route that forwards the request. Absent for the discovery locator.

discoveryLocator.description: True when the gateway's discovery locator forwards the request, not a route.

url.description: Where the gateway forwards the request: the route's URI, or lb:// and the service ID for the discovery locator.

source.description: The entity ID of the route's code or module, or of the module whose config turns the discovery locator on.

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts it comes from: the endpoint and the route, or the endpoint, the discovery locator's config and the target's name, in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone it holds. Absent when it holds in the default view.

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which it does not hold. Absent when it holds under every profile.

name: shared-secret
description: The subject unit signs or checks JWTs with an HMAC secret that other units have too (with), for the findings page: their secrets come from the same placeholder nothing resolves (the environment fills one value in for all), the same config value, or, when the value is masked or unset, the same config key. The value is the config keys the unit reads the secret from; the secret's value is never recorded (ADR 0085).

basis.description: Why the secret is taken to be the same: placeholder, value or key (the weakest, confidence 0.7 of the fact's).

source.description: The entity ID of the method that makes the key (its jwt-secret-key fact).

library.description: The JWT library the method uses.

with.description: The entity IDs of the other units with the same secret.

uses.description: What the unit's code does with JWTs: sign, verify or both.

placeholders.description: For basis placeholder: the placeholders, as relaxed binding reads them (auth.token.signing.key for AUTH_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY).

link.description: No longer given since #576: the claim ID is the link's stable ID (ADR 0095). Kept so links stored before stay valid.

facts.description: The IDs of the facts it comes from: the jwt-secret-key facts of every unit with the secret and the unit's config values, in every view it holds in.

profile.description: The Spring profile under which alone the link holds, so it is conditional. Absent when it holds in the default view.

exceptProfiles.description: The profiles under which a link found in the default view does not hold, because the code or config of one of its ends is different or switched off there. Absent when it holds under every profile.

name: deployed-in
description: A container a deployment descriptor runs the subject in (a deployable unit, a frontend built from its folder, a data store on a database or Redis container, or an external identity provider on its container); the value names the environment, such as Docker Compose (local). The linker ties a container to a unit by name, and to a data store through the unit's datasource or Redis connection.

container.description: The container's name, the value of its deployment-container fact.

environment.description: The environment within its platform, as the deployment-container fact names it.

fact.description: The ID of the deployment-container fact.

name: outcome
description: What address resolution (#589) found an address to lead to when it is no unit or external system: outcome:ambiguous (several units, its candidates listed) or outcome:unknown.
